passes: First line contains conflict rather than biography.
Only Zhou Ye needs to be remembered by name.
PhD status and zero-paper pressure leak through interview dialogue.
Reliability is shown through failure_log and unfinished TODO rather than narrator explanation.
Physical space and small interruptions provide camera-like movement.
The scene advances a real external consequence: final interview invitation.
risks: The opening enters the interview room too quickly and does not yet give the reader a larger world/background frame.
Too many interviewer questions arrive in a clean sequence; the exchange risks feeling like a crafted oral exam.
Technical content can still dominate before the reader has emotional orientation.
The final email payoff is useful but slightly neat; later versions should preserve uncertainty around what exactly was rewarded.
The two unnamed interviewers are differentiated mainly by question timing rather than physical/social presence.
revision_direction: Add a short prelude image of the 2027 graduation/recruitment season: packing labs, destination forms, job notices, people waiting to be priced by organizations.
Cut one or two technical Q&A chains and replace with interruption, hesitation or misreading.
Keep no more than one explicit background datum per exchange.
Do not name the macro theme 'first pricing' in prose.
Keep the final-interview notification but make it feel like one door opening rather than moral reward.

comparison_to_old_opening.judgment: new entrance is substantially more novelistic because the reader meets Zhou under external pressure rather than watching him self-construct a portfolio in isolation.
